style.a: Idempotency means that sending the same request multiple times produces the same final state as sending it once, even if the intermediate responses differ. GET, PUT, DELETE, and POST with an idempotent body are idempotent by design; POST that creates a new record is not, because repeated sends create multiple records. Idempotency protects against retries and network failures, but it does not make a request atomic: concurrent requests can still race and corrupt state unless the server coordinates them.

A secret committed to git is stored in the repository history, which is immutable and shared with every clone, so it can leak through commits, tags, branches, and backups. The immediate risk is exposure in the repository, and the long-term risk is that it remains in history even after deletion. The fix is to prevent secrets from entering the repository in the first place, for example through a secret manager, a pre-commit guard, or a .gitignore entry for credential files.

Python threads share the global interpreter, so CPU-bound work is not automatically parallelized across cores. Multiprocessing spawns separate processes, each with its own interpreter and memory, and can use all available cores. The trade-off is interprocess communication, which is slower than thread-local data, plus fork-based startup on Unix and start-up overhead on Windows. Multiprocessing is therefore the right tool for CPU-bound tasks, not for I/O-bound ones where threads or asyncio are preferable.

Un load balancer distribuisce le richieste tra più istanze, per evitare che una sola riceva tutto il carico. Usa algoritmi diversi: round robin, che gira per istanza in ordine; least connections, che manda il traffico sull'istanza con meno connessioni attive; e ip, che usa l'indirizzo IP come hash per mantenere lo stesso cliente sullo stesso nodo. Il vantaggio è che se un nodo si guasta, gli altri continuano a servire, e il carico si bilancia anche tra server con capacità diverse.
